title.zh: 卷九 陳本紀上第九 武帝 文帝 廢帝
title.en: Volume 9 Chen Annals 1: Emperor Wu, Emperor Wen, Deposed Emperor
title.raw: 卷九 陳本紀上第九 武帝 文帝 廢帝 Volume 9 Chen Annals 1: Emperor Wu, Emperor Wen, Deposed Emperor

sentences.zh: 陳本紀上第九

translations.literal: Chen Annals, Upper Fascicle Nine
translations.idiomatic: Chen Annals 1, Part Nine

sentences.zh: 陳高祖武皇帝諱霸先，字興國，小字法生，吳興長城下若里人。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, Martial Emperor of Chen, taboo name Baxian, courtesy name Xingguo, childhood name Fasheng, was a native of Xiaru Village, Changcheng, Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's founding emperor Wu, personal name Baxian, style Xingguo, childhood name Fasheng, came from Xiaru Village in Changcheng, Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 姓陳氏。

translations.literal: His surname was Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The clan name was Chen.

sentences.zh: 其本甚微，自雲漢太丘長寔之後也。

translations.literal: His origin was very humble; he traced descent from Shi of the Han dynasty, Grand Commandant of Taiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The family was of humble stock, claiming descent from Shi, Grand Commandant of Taiqiu in the Han.

sentences.zh: 寔玄孫晉太尉准。

translations.literal: Shi's great-great-grandson was Zhun, Grand Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's fourth-generation descendant was Jin Grand Commandant Zhun.

sentences.zh: 准生匡，匡生達，永嘉中南遷，為丞相掾，太子洗馬，出為長城令，悅其山水，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Zhun begot Kuang; Kuang begot Da. In the Yongjia era they migrated south, served as clerks to the Chancellor, as Palace Groom of the Heir Apparent, and were sent out as magistrate of Changcheng; delighted in its mountains and waters, they made it their home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun's son was Kuang, Kuang's son Da. During the Yongjia turmoil they moved south, held posts as chancellor's clerk and crown prince's groom, and were eventually posted as magistrate of Changcheng, where they settled for love of the landscape.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「此地山川秀麗，當有王者興焉，二百年後，我子孫必鍾斯運。

translations.literal: Once he said to those close to him: "This place's mountains and rivers are fair; a king will surely rise here. Two hundred years hence, my descendants will surely meet this destiny.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his intimates: "These hills and streams are splendid; a ruler will one day arise here. Two centuries from now our line will surely seize that fortune.

sentences.zh: 」達生康，復為丞相掾，咸和中土斷，故為長城人。

translations.literal: " Da begot Kang, again served as chancellor's clerk; in the Xianhe era the land registers were severed, hence they became men of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: " Da's son Kang again served as a chancellor's clerk; after the Xianhe land registers were cut off, the family counted as Changcheng natives.

sentences.zh: 康生盱眙太守英，英生尚書郎公弼，公弼生步兵校尉鼎，鼎生散騎侍郎高，高生懷安令詠，詠生安成太守猛，猛生太常卿道巨，道巨生皇考文贊。

translations.literal: Kang begot Ying, Administrator of Xuyi; Ying begot Gongbi, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; Gongbi begot Ding, Colonel of Foot Soldiers; Ding begot Gao, Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; Gao begot Yong, Magistrate of Huai'an; Yong begot Meng, Administrator of Ancheng; Meng begot Daoju, Minister of Ceremonies; Daoju begot the late Emperor's father Wenzan.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's son Ying became Administrator of Xuyi; Ying's son Gongbi was a Masters of Writing gentleman; Gongbi's son Ding was Colonel of Foot Soldiers; Ding's son Gao was an attendant at the Secretariat; Gao's son Yong was magistrate of Huai'an; Yong's son Meng was administrator of Ancheng; Meng's son Daoju was Minister of Ceremonies; Daoju was the Emperor's father Wenzan.

sentences.zh: 帝以梁天監二年癸未歲生。

translations.literal: The Emperor was born in the year guiwei, second year of Tianjian of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was born in guiwei, the second year of Liang Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 少俶儻有大志，長於謀略，意氣雄傑，不事生產。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited with great ambition, skilled in strategy, bold and heroic in spirit, and did not engage in farming or trade.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was daring and ambitious, excelled at strategy, carried himself with heroic force, and scorned the work of making a living.

sentences.zh: 及長，涉獵史籍，好讀兵書，明緯候、孤虛、遁甲之術，多武藝，明達果斷，為當時推服。

translations.literal: When grown, he ranged through historical records, loved reading military texts, understood the arts of weft-and-woof portents, guxu, and dunjia, possessed many martial skills, was clear-sighted and resolute, and was admired by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown he read widely in history, devoured military classics, mastered omen-reading, guxu divination, and dunjia tactics, was versed in many martial arts, and proved clear-minded and decisive—qualities that won the age's respect.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺五寸，日角龍顏，垂手過膝。

translations.literal: His height was seven chi five cun; he had a sun-cornered, dragon-faced countenance, and his hands hung past his knees.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi five cun tall, bore the sun-angled brow and dragon visage of portent, and his fingertips reached below his knees.

sentences.zh: 嘗游義興，館于許氏，夢天開數丈，有四人朱衣，捧日而至，納之帝口，及覺，腹內猶熱，帝心獨喜。

translations.literal: Once traveling in Yixing, he lodged with the Xu clan; he dreamed the sky opened several zhang, four men in red robes bearing the sun came to him and placed it in the Emperor's mouth; upon waking, his belly was still warm, and the Emperor rejoiced alone.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling in Yixing and staying with the Xu family, he dreamed the heavens split open several zhang wide; four men in crimson robes bore the sun to him and put it in his mouth. When he woke his abdomen still burned with heat, and he kept the joy to himself.

sentences.zh: 初仕鄉為裏司，後至建鄴為油庫吏，徙為新喻侯蕭映傳教，勤於其事，為映所賞。

translations.literal: At first he served in the district as village officer; later he reached Jiankang as clerk of the oil depot, was transferred to serve as instructor under the Marquis of Xinyu, Xiao Ying, was diligent in his duties, and was appreciated by Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He first served locally as a village officer, later reached Jiankang as clerk of the oil depot, then became instructor to Marquis Xinyu Xiao Ying, whose trust he earned through tireless service.

sentences.zh: 及映為吳興太守，甚重帝，謂僚佐曰：「此人將來遠大，必勝於我。

translations.literal: When Ying became Administrator of Wuxing, he greatly valued the Emperor and told his staff: "This man's future will be far-reaching; he will surely surpass me.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying became administrator of Wuxing he held the Emperor in high regard and told his aides: "This man's horizon stretches far; he will outdo me one day.

sentences.zh: 」及映為廣州，帝為中直兵參軍，隨之鎮，映令帝招集士馬。

translations.literal: " When Ying went to Guangzhou, the Emperor served as Central Straight Army Adjutant, followed him to the garrison, and Ying ordered the Emperor to gather soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ying took Guangzhou, the Emperor followed as adjutant of the central straight guard; Ying ordered him to raise troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 先是武林侯蕭諮為交州刺史，以嚴刻失和，土人李賁連結數州豪傑同時反，台遣高州刺史孫冏、新州刺史盧子雄將兵擊賁。

translations.literal: Earlier the Marquis of Wulin, Xiao Zi, had been Inspector of Jiaozhou; through severity he lost harmony, and the native Li Ben linked several prefectures' worth of local magnates in simultaneous revolt; the court sent Sun Tong, Inspector of Gaozhou, and Lu Zixiong, Inspector of Xinzhou, with troops to strike Ben.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Marquis Wulin Xiao Zi, as inspector of Jiaozhou, had alienated the region by harsh rule; the local leader Li Ben rallied magnates across several prefectures in revolt, and the court dispatched Gaozhou inspector Sun Tong and Xinzhou inspector Lu Zixiong against him.

sentences.zh: 冏等不時進，皆于廣州伏誅。

translations.literal: Tong and the others did not advance in time; all were executed at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong and his colleagues failed to advance promptly and were all put to death at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子雄弟子略與冏子侄及其主帥杜天合、杜僧明共舉兵，執南江督護沈顗，進寇廣州，晝夜苦攻，州中震恐。

translations.literal: Zixiong's nephew's son Lue, together with Tong's sons and nephews and their commanders Du Tianhe and Du Sengming, all raised troops, seized the Southern River Supervisor Shen Yan, advanced to raid Guangzhou, and day and night pressed the attack; the province was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zixiong's nephew Lue joined Sun Tong's kin and their generals Du Tianhe and Du Sengming in rebellion, seized Southern River supervisor Shen Yan, and besieged Guangzhou day and night until the city trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 帝率精兵救之，賊眾大潰。

translations.literal: The Emperor led elite troops to rescue it; the rebel host was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led picked troops to the relief of Guangzhou and shattered the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 僧明後有功業，遂降。

translations.literal: Sengming later achieved merit and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Du Sengming later won distinction in service and submitted.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝深歎異焉，授直合將軍，封新安縣子，仍遣圖帝貌而觀之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply marveled at this, appointed him General of the Direct Guard, enfeoffed him as Baron of Xin'an, and moreover sent someone to paint his likeness and observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang was deeply impressed, made him General of the Direct Guard, created him Baron of Xin'an, and even ordered his portrait painted for inspection.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，侯景寇逼，帝將赴援，廣州刺史元景仲陰將圖帝。

translations.literal: In the second year, winter, Hou Jing pressed close in invasion; the Emperor was about to go to the rescue when Inspector of Guangzhou Yuan Jingzhong secretly plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, winter, as Hou Jing's invasion closed in, the Emperor prepared to march to the rescue, but Guangzhou inspector Yuan Jingzhong secretly plotted his downfall.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，與成州刺史王懷明等，集兵於南海，馳檄以討景仲。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it; with Administrator of Chengzhou Wang Huaiming and others he gathered troops at Nanhai and dispatched a proclamation to punish Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, he joined Chengzhou administrator Wang Huaiming and others at Nanhai and issued a summons to punish Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 景仲縊於合下，帝迎蕭勃鎮廣州。

translations.literal: Jingzhong hanged himself beneath the gate-tower; the Emperor welcomed Xiao Bo to garrison Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong hanged himself under the gate-tower; the Emperor then installed Xiao Bo as garrison commander of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時臨賀內史歐陽頠監衡州，蘭裕、蘭京禮扇誘始興等十郡共攻頠，頠請援於勃，勃令帝救之，悉禽裕等。

translations.literal: At that time Interior Secretary Ouyang Yu supervised Heng Province; Lan Yu and Lan Jingli incited and enticed Shixing and ten other commanderies to attack Yu jointly; Yu requested aid from Bo, and Bo ordered the Emperor to save him; all of Yu and the others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: At that time interior secretary Ouyang Yu held Hengzhou; Lan Yu and Lan Jingli stirred Shixing and ten neighboring commanderies into joint attack. Yu appealed to Bo, who sent the Emperor to relieve him; Yu and his allies were all taken.

sentences.zh: 仍監始興郡事。

translations.literal: He was then made supervisor of Shixing commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then put in charge of Shixing commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝遣杜僧明、胡穎將二千人頓於嶺上，並厚結始興豪傑，同謀義舉，侯安都、張偲等率眾來附。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Du Sengming and Hu Ying with two thousand men to encamp on the ridge, and also richly allied with Shixing magnates in a planned righteous rising; Hou Andu, Zhang Si, and others led crowds to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor posted Du Sengming and Hu Ying with two thousand men on the mountain pass and won over Shixing's leading families for a righteous uprising; Hou Andu, Zhang Si, and others brought their followers over.

sentences.zh: 蕭勃聞之，遣鍾休悅說停帝，帝泣謂休悅曰：「君辱臣死，誰敢愛命，僕行計決矣。

translations.literal: When Xiao Bo heard of it, he sent Zhong Xiuyue to persuade the Emperor to stop; the Emperor wept and told Xiuyue: "When the lord is shamed, the minister must die—who would spare his life? My course is set.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo sent Zhong Xiuyue to dissuade him; the Emperor wept and said: "When one's lord is disgraced, his servant must die—who clings to life? My mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 」時蔡路養起兵據南康，勃遣腹心譚世遠為曲江令，與路養相結，同遏義軍。

translations.literal: " At that time Cai Luyang raised troops and held Nankang; Bo sent his trusted man Tan Shiyuan as magistrate of Qujiang to ally with Luyang and together block the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile Cai Luyang seized Nankang; Bo sent his confidant Tan Shiyuan as magistrate of Qujiang to join Luyang in blocking the loyalist force.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年正月，帝發始興，次大庾嶺，大破路養軍，進頓南康。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dabao, the Emperor set out from Shixing, halted at Dayu Ridge, thoroughly defeated Luyang's army, and advanced to encamp at Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dabao 1 the Emperor marched from Shixing, camped at Dayu Ridge, broke Luyang's army, and pressed on to Nankang.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹承制授帝交州刺史，改封南野縣伯，於是修理崎頭古城徙居之。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong Xiao Yi, acting on imperial commission, appointed the Emperor Inspector of Jiaozhou and changed his enfeoffment to Earl of Nanye; he then repaired the old city at Qitou and moved to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong Xiao Yi, exercising imperial authority, made him inspector of Jiaozhou and raised his title to Earl of Nanye; he restored the old fortress at Qitou and made it his seat.

sentences.zh: 劉惠騫等望見恒有紫氣冒城上，遠近驚異，故惠騫等深自結於帝。

translations.literal: Liu Huiqian and others, seeing from afar that purple vapor constantly covered the city, were astonished near and far; hence Huiqian and the others deeply attached themselves to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huiqian and others saw purple mist perpetually shrouding the city from afar and were awestruck; they therefore bound themselves closely to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋改封長城縣侯，南江州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Changcheng and made Inspector of the Southern River.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon re-created Marquis of Changcheng and named inspector of the Southern River.

sentences.zh: 時甯都人劉藹等資高州刺史李遷仕舟艦兵仗，將襲南康，帝遣杜僧明等據白口禦。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Ai of Ningdu and others supplied Inspector of Gaozhou Li Qianshi with warships and arms, intending to strike Nankang; the Emperor sent Du Sengming and others to hold Baikou in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Ai of Ningdu and others armed Gaozhou inspector Li Qianshi with ships and weapons for a strike on Nankang; the Emperor sent Du Sengming to hold Baikou.

sentences.zh: 二年，僧明禽遷仕，送南康斬之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Sengming captured Qianshi, sent him to Nankang, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Du Sengming captured Qianshi, brought him to Nankang, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 承制授帝江州刺史。

translations.literal: Acting on commission, he was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial commission he became inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝發南康，灨石舊有二十四灘，灘多巨石，行旅以為難。

translations.literal: The Emperor set out from Nankang; at Gan Rock there had formerly been twenty-four rapids, the rapids holding many boulders, and travelers considered the route difficult.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor marched from Nankang, Gan Rock still held its twenty-four shoals of boulders that travelers had long dreaded.

sentences.zh: 帝之發，水暴起數丈，三百里間，巨石皆沒。

translations.literal: When the Emperor set out, the waters suddenly rose several zhang; within three hundred li all the boulders were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed the waters surged several zhang, and for three hundred li every boulder sank from sight.

sentences.zh: 進軍頓西昌，有龍見水濱，高五丈，五采鮮曜，軍民觀者數萬人。

translations.literal: Advancing he encamped at Xichang; a dragon appeared at the water's edge, five zhang high, its five colors bright and dazzling; soldiers and civilians numbering tens of thousands watched.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Xichang, where a dragon five zhang tall appeared at the riverbank in blazing five-colored light before tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 帝又嘗獨坐胡床於合下，忽有神光滿合，廊廡之間，並得相見。

translations.literal: The Emperor also once sat alone on a folding stool beneath the gate-tower; suddenly divine light filled the hall, and even the corridors could be seen through it.
translations.idiomatic: He also once sat alone on a camp stool beneath the gate-tower when divine radiance flooded the hall and lit even the side galleries.

sentences.zh: 趙知禮侍側，怪而問帝，帝笑不答。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhili attended at his side, wondered, and asked the Emperor; the Emperor smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhili, attending beside him, asked in astonishment; the Emperor only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 時承制遣征東將軍王僧辯督眾軍討侯景，次盆城，帝率杜僧明等合三萬人將會焉。

translations.literal: At that time, acting on commission, General Who Conquers the East Wang Sengbian was dispatched to supervise the armies in punishing Hou Jing, halting at Pencheng; the Emperor led Du Sengming and others with thirty thousand men to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Then, by commission, Wang Sengbian, General Who Conquers the East, was leading the armies against Hou Jing at Pencheng; the Emperor brought Du Sengming and thirty thousand men to rendezvous with him.

sentences.zh: 時西軍乏食，帝先貯軍糧五十萬石，至是分三十萬石以資之。

translations.literal: At that time the western army lacked food; the Emperor had stored fifty thousand shi of grain beforehand; upon arrival he divided out three hundred thousand shi to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The western army was starving; the Emperor had stored fifty thousand shi of grain and now shared thirty thousand shi with them.

sentences.zh: 仍頓巴丘。

translations.literal: He then encamped at Baqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He then halted at Baqiu.

sentences.zh: 會侯景廢簡文，立豫章嗣王棟，帝遣兼長史沈袞奉表於江陵勸進。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and established Prince of Yuzhang, the Heir Dong, the Emperor sent Acting Chief Clerk Shen Gun to present a memorial at Jiangling urging advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and set up Prince Yuzhang Dong as heir, the Emperor sent acting chief clerk Shen Gun to Jiangling with a memorial urging enthronement.

sentences.zh: 承制授帝東揚州刺史，領會稽太守。

translations.literal: Acting on commission, he was appointed Inspector of Dongyang and concurrently Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: By commission he became inspector of Dongyang and concurrently administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝帥師發自豫章。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Emperor led the army setting out from Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Emperor led his army out from Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 二月，次桑落洲。

translations.literal: In the second month, he halted at Sangluo Isle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he stopped at Sangluo Isle.

sentences.zh: 時僧辯已發盆城，會帝于白茅灣，乃登岸結壇，刑牲盟約。

translations.literal: At that time Sengbian had already set out from Pencheng; he met the Emperor at Baimao Bay; they then went ashore, raised an altar, and sacrificed animals in covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian had already marched from Pencheng and met him at Baimao Bay; they went ashore, built an altar, and swore their alliance with sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 進次大雷，軍人杜棱夢雷池君、周、何神，自稱征討大將軍，乘朱航，陳甲仗，稱下征侯景，須臾便還，雲已殺景竟。

translations.literal: Advancing he halted at Dalei; the soldier Du Ling dreamed the Lord of Lei Pool and the gods Zhou and He, calling themselves Great Generals of Punitive Campaign, rode a vermilion vessel with armor displayed, saying they descended to punish Hou Jing; in a moment they returned, saying Jing was already killed.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Dalei, soldier Du Ling dreamed the Lord of Lei Pool and the gods Zhou and He, calling themselves punitive grand generals, came in a crimson boat in full armor to chastise Hou Jing, then swiftly returned declaring Jing already slain.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝與諸軍進克姑孰，仍次蔡洲。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Emperor with the armies advanced and captured Gushu, then halted at Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the allied armies took Gushu and camped at Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 侯景登石頭城，望官軍之盛，不悅，曰：「一把子人，何足可打。

translations.literal: Hou Jing ascended Shitou city, looked upon the splendor of the imperial army, and was displeased, saying: "A handful of men—what is there worth striking?
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing climbed Shitou and, seeing the imperial host's might, muttered in displeasure: "A fistful of men—hardly worth a fight.

sentences.zh: 」密謂左右曰：「此軍上有紫氣，不易可當。

translations.literal: " Secretly he told those beside him: "Above this army there is purple vapor; it will not be easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: " He whispered to his attendants: "Purple mist hangs over that host—not easily resisted.

sentences.zh: 」乃以貓琉貯石，沈塞淮口，緣淮作城，自石頭迄青溪十餘里中，樓雉相接。

translations.literal: " He then stored stones in cat-litter containers, sank them to block the Huai mouth, and along the Huai built a wall from Shitou to Qingxi for more than ten li, with towers and battlements joined.
translations.idiomatic: " He filled litter boxes with stone, sank them to choke the Huai mouth, and raised a wall with linked towers from Shitou to Qingxi for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 僧辯遣杜崱問計於帝，帝以諸將不敢當鋒，請先往立柵。

translations.literal: Sengbian sent Du Yan to ask the Emperor's plan; the Emperor, because the generals dared not meet the enemy's edge, requested to go first and establish palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian sent Du Yan for counsel; since no general would meet the enemy head-on, the Emperor offered to go forward and throw up palisades.

sentences.zh: 即於石頭西橫壟築柵。

translations.literal: Immediately at the western bridge of Shitou he built a palisade across the mound.
translations.idiomatic: At once he raised a palisade across the mound west of Shitou's bridge.

sentences.zh: 眾軍次連八城，直出東北。

translations.literal: The mass of armies halted in succession at eight cities, thrusting straight out to the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: The allied columns linked eight fortified positions in a line thrusting northeast.

sentences.zh: 賊恐西州路斷，亦于東北果林作五城，以遏大路。

translations.literal: The rebels feared the western route would be cut; they also built five cities in the northeast fruit groves to block the main road.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing severance of the western route, the rebels too threw up five forts in the northeast orchards to choke the highway.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善用兵者，如常山之蛇，使救首救尾，困而無暇。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "One who uses troops well is like the snake of Mount Chang—strike the head and the tail saves it, strike the tail and the head saves it, trapping the foe without leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "A master of war is like Mount Chang's serpent—strike the head and the tail responds, strike the tail and the head responds, keeping the enemy too busy to breathe.

sentences.zh: 今我師既眾，賊徒甚寡，應分賊兵力，以強制弱。

translations.literal: Now our host is numerous and the rebels few; we should divide the rebels' strength and use strength to overcome weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Our force is many and theirs few; we should split their strength and crush weakness with strength.

sentences.zh: 」乃命諸將分處置兵，帝與王琳、杜龕等悉力乘之，景眾大潰。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the generals to deploy troops separately; the Emperor with Wang Lin, Du Kan, and others pressed with full force, and Jing's host was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: " He dispersed his generals; then he, Wang Lin, Du Kan, and others drove home the attack and Hou Jing's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 僧辯啟命帝鎮京口。

translations.literal: Sengbian memorialized ordering the Emperor to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian memorialized that the Emperor should hold Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 五月，齊遣將辛術圍嚴超達于秦郡，帝命徐度領兵助其固守。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Qi sent General Xin Shu to besiege Yan Chaoda at Qin commandery; the Emperor ordered Xu Du to lead troops to help him hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Northern Qi general Xin Shu besieged Yan Chaoda at Qin commandery; the Emperor sent Xu Du to reinforce the defense.

sentences.zh: 齊眾起土山，穿地道，攻之甚急；

translations.literal: The Qi host raised earthen mounds and dug underground passages, pressing the attack very urgently;
translations.idiomatic: The Qi army piled earthworks and dug tunnels, pressing the siege relentlessly;

sentences.zh: 帝乃自率萬人解其圍，振旅南歸。

translations.literal: the Emperor then personally led ten thousand men to lift the siege and returned south with his army refreshed.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor then led ten thousand men in person to break the encirclement and marched south in good order.

sentences.zh: 承制授帝征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史，進封長城縣公。

translations.literal: Acting on commission, he was appointed Grand General Who Conquers the North, Commissioner with the insignia of Grand Prefect of the Three Offices, and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: By commission he became Grand General Who Conquers the North, Commissioner with Grand Prefect insignia, inspector of Southern Xuzhou, and was advanced to Duke of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 及王僧辯征陸納於湘州，承制命帝代鎮揚州。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Lu Na in Xiang Province, acting on commission the Emperor was ordered to replace him in garrisoning Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian marched against Lu Na in Xiangzhou, the Emperor was commissioned to replace him as garrison commander of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，湘州平，帝旋鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, Xiang Province was pacified; the Emperor returned to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng 2, with Xiangzhou pacified, he returned to hold Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，進帝位司空。

translations.literal: In the third year, third month, the Emperor was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, third month, he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及魏平江陵，帝與王僧辯等進啟請晉安王乙太宰承制。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, the Emperor with Wang Sengbian and others submitted a memorial requesting Prince Jin'an Yi as Grand Preceptor exercising imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei captured Jiangling, he and Wang Sengbian memorialized for Prince Jin'an Yi to serve as Grand Preceptor with imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉安王至自尋陽，入居朝堂，給帝班劍二十人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Prince Jin'an arrived from Xunyang and entered the court hall; the Emperor was granted twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince Jin'an arrived from Xunyang and took the court hall; the Emperor received twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 震州刺史杜龕據吳興，與義興太守韋載舉兵逆命。

translations.literal: Du Kan, Inspector of Zhenzhou, held Wuxing; Administrator of Yixing Wei Zai raised troops in disobedience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou inspector Du Kan held Wuxing while Yixing administrator Wei Zai rebelled.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝表自東討，留高州刺史侯安都、石州刺史杜棱宿衛台省。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Emperor memorialized that he would personally campaign eastward; he left Hou Andu, Inspector of Gaozhou, and Du Ling, Inspector of Shizhou, to guard the capital offices.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he memorialized for a personal eastern campaign, leaving Gaozhou inspector Hou Andu and Shizhou inspector Du Ling to guard the capital offices.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，軍至義興。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the army reached Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the army reached Yixing.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史徐嗣徽，據城入齊，又要南豫州刺史任約舉兵應龕，齊人資其兵食。

translations.literal: Xu Sihui, Inspector of Qinzhou, entered the city and submitted to Qi, also summoning Ren Yue, Inspector of Southern Yu Province, to raise troops in response to Kan; the Qi people supplied them with troops and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou inspector Xu Sihui surrendered his city to Qi and summoned Southern Yuzhou inspector Ren Yue to revolt in support of Du Kan; Qi supplied both with troops and grain.

sentences.zh: 嗣徽乘虛奄至闕下，侯安都出戰，嗣徽等退據石頭。

translations.literal: Sihui seized the opportunity and suddenly reached beneath the palace gates; Hou Andu went out to battle; Sihui and the others withdrew to hold Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui stole up to the palace gates; Hou Andu sallied forth and drove him back to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，載及龕從弟北叟來降，帝撫而釋之，仍以載兄鼎知郡事。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Zai and Kan's younger cousin Beisou came to surrender; the Emperor comforted and released them, and still made Zai's elder brother Ding administer the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wei Zai and Du Kan's cousin Beisou surrendered; the Emperor pardoned them and put Zai's brother Ding in charge of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 以嗣徽寇逼，卷甲還都，命周文育進討杜龕。

translations.literal: Because Sihui's raid pressed close, he rolled up his armor and returned to the capital, ordering Zhou Wenyu to advance and punish Du Kan.
translations.idiomatic: With Sihui threatening the capital he turned back in haste and ordered Zhou Wenyu forward against Du Kan.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，齊遣兵五千，度據姑孰，又遣安州刺史翟子崇、楚州刺史劉士榮、淮州刺史柳達摩，領兵萬人，于胡墅度米粟三萬石、馬千匹入石頭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jimao, Qi sent five thousand troops who crossed and held Gushu; they also sent Anzhou Inspector Zhai Zichong, Chuzhou Inspector Liu Shirong, and Huaizhou Inspector Liu Damo with ten thousand troops; at Husi they crossed thirty thousand shi of grain and rice and a thousand horses into Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, jimao, Qi sent five thousand men to cross and seize Gushu, and Anzhou inspector Zhai Zichong, Chuzhou inspector Liu Shirong, and Huaizhou inspector Liu Damo with ten thousand troops ferried thirty thousand shi of grain and a thousand horses into Shitou at Husi.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣侯安都領水軍夜襲胡墅，燒齊船，周鐵武率舟師斷齊運輸，帝領鐵騎自西明門襲之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent Hou Andu leading the navy in a night raid on Husi, burning Qi ships; Zhou Tiewu led the fleet to cut Qi transport; the Emperor himself led iron cavalry from the Western Bright Gate to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hou Andu's fleet to burn Qi ships at Husi by night, Zhou Tiewu to sever their supply line, and himself led iron cavalry from the Western Bright Gate in the assault.

sentences.zh: 齊人大潰，嗣徽留達摩等守城，自率親屬腹心，往南州採石，以迎齊援。

translations.literal: The Qi host was utterly routed; Sihui left Damo and others to hold the city and personally led kin and trusted followers south to Caishi in Nan Province to meet Qi reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was routed; Sihui left Damo to hold the city and raced south to Caishi to meet Qi reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 先是，太白自十一月丙戌不見，十二月乙卯出於東方。

translations.literal: Earlier, from bingxu in the eleventh month Venus had not been seen; on yimao in the twelfth month it appeared in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Venus had vanished since bingxu in the eleventh month; on yimao in the twelfth it reappeared in the east.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝盡命眾軍分部甲卒，對冶城立航，度兵攻其水南二柵。

translations.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor fully ordered the armies to divide armor and troops, build bridges opposite Ye City, and cross troops to attack the two palisades south of the water.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he divided the host, bridged opposite Ye City, and sent troops against the two palisades south of the river.

sentences.zh: 柳達摩等度淮置陣，帝督兵疾戰，縱火燒柵，煙塵漲天，齊人大潰，盡收其船艦。

translations.literal: Liu Damo and others crossed the Huai and set battle lines; the Emperor supervised the troops in fierce fighting, set fire and burned the palisades; smoke and dust filled the sky; the Qi host was utterly routed and all their ships were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Damo crossed the Huai and formed line; the Emperor fought fiercely, torched the palisades until smoke blotted the sky, routed Qi, and seized every ship.

sentences.zh: 是日，嗣徽、約等領齊兵還據石頭，帝遣侯安都領水軍襲破之，嗣徽等單舸脫走。

translations.literal: That day, Sihui, Yue, and others led Qi troops back to hold Shitou; the Emperor sent Hou Andu leading the navy to raid and break them; Sihui and the others escaped in single boats.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Sihui and Yue brought Qi troops back to Shitou; Hou Andu's fleet smashed them and they fled in lone boats.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，拔石頭南岸柵，移度北岸起柵，以絕其汲路。

translations.literal: On dingsi, they captured the southern-bank palisade of Shitou, moved across to the north bank and raised palisades, cutting off their water route.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi they took Shitou's south-bank palisade, crossed to the north bank, and walled off the water supply.

sentences.zh: 又堙塞東門故城中諸井。

translations.literal: They also filled in all the wells in the old city's eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: They also choked every well in the old city's east gate quarter.

sentences.zh: 齊所據城中無水，水一合貿米一升，一升米貿絹一匹，或炒米食之。

translations.literal: In the city held by Qi there was no water; one he of water traded for one sheng of rice, one sheng of rice traded for one bolt of silk, or they ate fried rice.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's garrison ran dry; a cup of water bought a pint of rice, a pint of rice a bolt of silk, and some ground rice to eat.

sentences.zh: 達摩謂其眾曰：「頃在北，童謠雲，'石頭搗兩襠，搗青復搗黃 '。

translations.literal: Damo told his host: "Recently in the north, a children's song said, 'Shitou, pound two crotches—pound green, then pound yellow.'
translations.idiomatic: Damo told his men: "A northern children's song lately ran: 'Pound Shitou's britches—green first, then yellow.'"

sentences.zh: 侯景服青，已倒於此，今吾徒衣黃，豈謠言驗邪。

translations.literal: Hou Jing wore green and already fell here; now our crowd wears yellow—is the song fulfilled?
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing wore green and fell here; we wear yellow—does the rhyme come true?

sentences.zh: 」庚申，達摩遣侯子欽、劉士榮等請和，帝許之。

translations.literal: " On gengshen, Damo sent Hou Ziqin, Liu Shirong, and others to request peace; the Emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " On gengshen Damo sent Hou Ziqin and Liu Shirong to sue for peace, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃於城外盟約，其將士恣其南北。

translations.literal: They then made covenant outside the walls; their officers and soldiers went north and south as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: They swore peace outside the walls and let Qi soldiers go north or south freely.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，帝出石頭南門陳兵，送齊人歸北者。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Emperor deployed troops at Shitou's south gate and escorted those Qi men returning north.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou he drew up ranks at Shitou's south gate and escorted the Qi troops northward.

sentences.zh: 及至，齊人殺之。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the Qi men killed them.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the northerners slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，齊和州長史烏丸遠自南州奔還曆陽，江甯令陳嗣、黃門侍郎曹朗據姑孰，不從。

translations.literal: On renxu, Wuwan Yuan of Hezhou's Chief Clerk fled back from Nan Province to Liyang; Jiangning Magistrate Chen Si and Palace Attendant Cao Lang held Gushu and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Hezhou chief clerk Wuwan Yuan fled from Nan Province to Liyang; Jiangning magistrate Chen Si and palace attendant Cao Lang held Gushu in defiance.

sentences.zh: 帝命侯安都、徐度等討平之，聚其首為京觀。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Hou Andu, Xu Du, and others to punish and pacify them, piling their heads into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Hou Andu and Xu Du to crush them and piled their heads into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 是月，杜龕以城降。

translations.literal: That month, Du Kan surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: That month Du Kan surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 二年正月癸未，誅龕，其弟翕、從弟北叟、司馬沈孝敦並賜死。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on guiwei, Kan was executed; his younger brother Xi, cousin Beisou, and Chief Clerk Shen Xiaodun were all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year's first month, guiwei, Du Kan was executed; his brother Xi, cousin Beisou, and chief clerk Shen Xiaodun were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，齊遣水軍儀同蕭軌、庫狄伏連、堯難宗、東方老、侍中裴英起、東廣州刺史獨狐辟惡、洛州刺史李希光並任約、徐嗣徽、王僧愔等眾十萬出柵口，向梁山，帳內蕩主黃叢逆擊，敗之，燒其前軍船艦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuxu, Qi sent naval Commissioner of State Xiao Gui, Kudie Fulian, Yao Nanzong, Dongfang Lao, Palace Attendant Pei Yingqi, Eastern Guangzhou Inspector Dugu Pie'e, and Luozhou Inspector Li Xiguang, together with Ren Yue, Xu Sihui, Wang Sengyin, and others—one hundred thousand in all—out from Zhakou toward Liang Mountain; Huang Cong, chief of the tent guard, counterattacked, defeated them, and burned their vanguard ships.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the third month Qi sent Commissioner Xiao Gui, Kudie Fulian, Yao Nanzong, Dongfang Lao, Pei Yingqi, Eastern Guangzhou inspector Dugu Pie'e, Luozhou inspector Li Xiguang, and with them Ren Yue, Xu Sihui, Wang Sengyin—one hundred thousand men—from Zhakou toward Liang Mountain; tent-guard chief Huang Cong counterattacked, routed them, and burned the vanguard fleet.

sentences.zh: 齊頓軍保蕪湖。

translations.literal: Qi halted the army and held Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's army halted and fortified Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 五月丙申，齊兵至秣陵故城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingshen, Qi troops reached the old city of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the fifth month Qi reached old Moling.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝率宗室王侯及朝臣，于大司馬門外白虎闕下，刑牲告天，以齊人背約，發言慷慨，涕泗交流，士卒觀者益奮。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Emperor led the imperial clan, princes, and court ministers outside the Grand Marshal Gate beneath the White Tiger Watchtower, sacrificed animals and announced to Heaven that the Qi men had broken covenant; his words were impassioned, tears streaming; soldiers and onlookers were the more inspired.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Emperor led princes and ministers outside the Grand Marshal Gate beneath the White Tiger Tower, sacrificed to Heaven accusing Qi of breaking faith; he spoke with burning passion, wept openly, and the watching soldiers burned with new zeal.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，齊軍於秣陵故城，跨淮立橋柵，引度兵馬。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Qi army at the old city of Moling spanned the Huai with bridges and palisades, drawing troops across.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Qi bridged the Huai at old Moling and drew troops across behind palisades.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，自方山進及兒塘，游騎至台，都下震駭。

translations.literal: On guimao, advancing from Fang Mountain they reached Ertang; roaming cavalry reached the capital, and the metropolis was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, advancing from Fang Mountain to Ertang, Qi scouts reached the capital and the city quaked with fear.

sentences.zh: 帝潛以精卒三千配沈泰，度江襲齊行台趙彥深于瓜步，獲其舟粟。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly assigned three thousand picked troops to Shen Tai to cross the river and strike Qi's field headquarters under Zhao Yanshen at Guabu, seizing their boats and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor secretly gave Shen Tai three thousand elite troops to cross the river and strike Qi field marshal Zhao Yanshen at Guabu, capturing boats and grain.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，齊兵潛至鍾山龍尾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Qi troops secretly reached Zhong Mountain's Dragon Tail.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the sixth month Qi stole up to Dragon Tail on Zhong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丁未，進至莫府山。

translations.literal: On dingwei, they advanced to Mofu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei they reached Mofu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 帝遣錢明領水軍出江乘，要擊齊人糧運，盡獲之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Qian Ming leading the navy out from Jiangcheng to intercept Qi grain transport and captured it all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Qian Ming's fleet from Jiangcheng to cut Qi's grain convoys and seized them entire.

sentences.zh: 齊軍大餒，殺馬驢而食之。

translations.literal: The Qi army was greatly famished and killed horses and donkeys to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's army starved and slaughtered horses and donkeys for food.

sentences.zh: 壬子，齊軍至玄武湖西北莫府山南，將據北郊壇。

translations.literal: On renzi, the Qi army reached the northwest of Xuanwu Lake at the south of Mofu Mountain, about to seize the northern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Qi reached the northwest shore of Xuanwu Lake below Mofu Mountain, aiming to take the northern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 眾軍自覆舟東移，頓郊壇北，與齊人相對。

translations.literal: The mass of armies moved from east of Fuzhou and encamped north of the suburban altar, facing the Qi men.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies shifted east of Fuzhou and camped north of the suburban altar, squarely facing Qi.

sentences.zh: 其夜，大雨震電，暴風拔木，平地水丈餘。

translations.literal: That night, great rain, thunder, and lightning; violent wind uprooted trees; on level ground water stood more than one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: That night thunderous rain and gale uprooted trees and left a zhang of water on the flats.

sentences.zh: 齊軍晝夜坐立泥中，縣鬲以爨，足指皆爛。

translations.literal: The Qi army day and night sat and stood in mud, hung pots to cook; their toes all rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's men day and night stood in mud, cooking from hanging pots until their toes rotted away.

sentences.zh: 而台中及潮溝北，水退路燥，官軍每得番易。

translations.literal: Yet within the capital and north of Chaogou the water receded and the roads dried; the imperial army could rotate shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the capital and north of Chaogou the flood fell and roads dried, letting the imperial army rotate fresh units.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，少霽。

translations.literal: On jiayin, there was slight clearing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the sky briefly cleared.

sentences.zh: 是時食盡，調市人饋軍，皆是麥屑為飯，以荷葉裹而分給，間以麥絆，兵士皆困。

translations.literal: At that time food was exhausted; the market people were levied to feed the army—all was barley-bran rice wrapped in lotus leaves and distributed, mixed at times with barley husks; the soldiers were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran out; townsfolk were pressed to feed the army on barley-bran cakes wrapped in lotus leaves, sometimes laced with chaff, and the troops were spent.

sentences.zh: 會文帝遣送米三千石，鴨千頭，帝即炊米煮鴨，誓申一戰。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Wen sent three thousand shi of rice and a thousand ducks; the Emperor immediately cooked rice and boiled ducks and swore to fight one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wen sent three thousand shi of rice and a thousand ducks; the Emperor cooked them at once and vowed one decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 士及防身，計糧數臠，人人裹飯，婫以鴨肉。

translations.literal: Officers and personal guards counted rations by the slice; each man wrapped rice, stuffing it with duck meat.
translations.idiomatic: Officers rationed meat by the slice; every man packed rice stuffed with duck.

sentences.zh: 帝命眾軍蓐食，攻之，齊軍大潰。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the armies to eat at their mats and attack; the Qi army was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the host to eat at the ready and strike; Qi's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 執嗣徽及其弟嗣宗，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: They captured Sihui and his younger brother Sizong and beheaded them to proclaim.
translations.idiomatic: They took Xu Sihui and his brother Sizong and beheaded them as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 虜蕭軌、東方老、王敬寶、李希光、裴英起、王僧智等將帥四十六人。

translations.literal: They captured forty-six Qi generals including Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, Pei Yingqi, and Wang Sengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-six Qi commanders were taken, among them Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, Pei Yingqi, and Wang Sengzhi.

sentences.zh: 其軍士得竄至江者，縳筏以濟，中江而溺，流屍至京口者彌岸。

translations.literal: Qi soldiers who fled to the river were bound to rafts to cross; mid-river they drowned, and corpses floating to Jingkou filled the banks.
translations.idiomatic: Qi soldiers who reached the river tied rafts to cross, drowned midstream, and corpses choked the banks at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 惟任約、王僧愔獲免。

translations.literal: Only Ren Yue and Wang Sengyin escaped capture.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ren Yue and Wang Sengyin got away.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠云：「虜萬夫，入五湖，城南酒家使虜奴。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's song said: "A hundred thousand captives enter the Five Lakes; south of the city a tavern makes slaves of the captives.
translations.idiomatic: A children's song had run: "A hundred thousand barbarians enter the Five Lakes; south of the city tavernkeepers turn captives into slaves.

sentences.zh: 」自晉、宋以後，經絓在魏境江、淮以北，南人皆謂為虜，于時以賞俘貿酒者，一人裁得一醉。

translations.literal: " From Jin and Song onward, the garrison belt north of the Yangtze and Huai in Wei territory—southerners all called them captives; at that time one man bought with reward captives could barely get one drunk.
translations.idiomatic: " Since Jin and Song, lands north of the Yangtze and Huai in Wei's grip were called "barbarian country" by southerners; now one captive's bounty barely bought a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，眾軍出南州，燒賊舟。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the mass of armies went out to Nan Province and burned the rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the allied armies sailed to Nan Province and burned the enemy fleet.

sentences.zh: 己未，斬劉歸義、徐嗣產、傅野豬于建康市。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Liu Guiyi, Xu Sichan, and Fu Yezhu were beheaded in Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Liu Guiyi, Xu Sichan, and Fu Yezhu were executed in Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 是日解嚴。

translations.literal: That day martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: That day the capital stood down from alert.

sentences.zh: 庚申，誅蕭軌、東方老、王敬寶、李希光、裴英起等。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, Pei Yingqi, and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Xiao Gui, Dongfang Lao, Wang Jingbao, Li Xiguang, Pei Yingqi, and others were put to death.

sentences.zh: 二年正月壬寅，詔加帝班劍十人，並前為三十。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on renyin, an edict added ten ceremonial swords to the Emperor, thirty in all with those before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year's first month, renyin, an edict added ten ceremonial swords, thirty in total.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔贈皇兄道談南兗州刺史、長城縣公，諡曰昭烈。

translations.literal: On dingwei, an edict posthumously enfeoffed the Emperor's elder brother Daotan as Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and Duke of Changcheng, posthumous title Zhaolie.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei an edict posthumously created the Emperor's elder brother Daotan inspector of Southern Yanzhou and Duke of Changcheng, titled posthumously Zhaolie.

sentences.zh: 皇弟休先侍中、南徐州刺史、武康縣侯，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: The Emperor's younger brother Xiuxian, Attendant, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, Marquis of Wukang, posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiuxian, attendant and Southern Xuzhou inspector, Marquis of Wukang, was titled posthumously Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，遣兼侍中謁者僕射陸繕策拜長城縣夫人章氏為義興國夫人。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Acting Attendant and Master of Ceremonies Lu Yan was dispatched to invest the Duchess of Changcheng, Lady Zhang, as Lady of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin acting attendant and Master of Ceremonies Lu Yan was sent to invest Duchess Changcheng Lady Zhang as Lady of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔贈皇祖侍中、太常卿，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: On dingmao, an edict posthumously enfeoffed the imperial grandfather as Attendant and Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao an edict posthumously honored the imperial grandfather as attendant and Minister of Ceremonies, titled Xiao.

sentences.zh: 追封皇祖妣許氏吳郡嘉興縣君，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed the imperial grandfather's mother Lady Xu as Lady of Jiaxing, Wujun, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The grandfather's mother Lady Xu was posthumously created Lady of Jiaxing in Wujun, titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 皇妣張氏義興國太夫人，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: The imperial mother Lady Zhang, Grand Lady of Yixing, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial mother Lady Zhang, Grand Lady of Yixing, was titled posthumously Xuan.

sentences.zh: 二月庚午，蕭勃舉兵自廣州度嶺，頓南康，遣其將歐陽頠、傅泰及其子孜為前軍，至豫章，分屯要險，南江州刺史余孝頃起兵應勃，帝命周文育、侯安都率眾討平之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on gengwu, Xiao Bo raised troops from Guangzhou, crossed the ridge, encamped at Nankang, and sent his generals Ouyang Yu, Fu Tai, and his son Zi as vanguard to Yuzhang, dividing encampments at strategic points; Yu Xiaoxiang, Inspector of the Southern River, raised troops in response to Bo; the Emperor ordered Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu to lead troops to punish and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the second month Xiao Bo rebelled from Guangzhou, crossed the mountains, camped at Nankang, and sent Ouyang Yu, Fu Tai, and his son Zi ahead to Yuzhang while Southern River inspector Yu Xiaoxiang joined the revolt; the Emperor sent Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu to crush them.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，帝進位太傅，加黃鉞，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiawu, the Emperor was advanced to Grand Preceptor, given the yellow battle-axe, sword and shoes in the hall, no quickened step entering court, no name spoken when bowing in praise.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the eighth month he was promoted to Grand Preceptor with the yellow axe, permission to wear sword and shoes in court, to enter without hastening, and to be praised without naming.

sentences.zh: 丙申，加前後部羽葆、鼓吹。

translations.literal: On bingshen, front and rear feather-canopies and drum-and-pipe were added.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen front and rear feather parasols and drum-and-pipe escort were added.

sentences.zh: 是時，湘州刺史王琳擁兵不應命，遣周文育、侯安都率眾討之。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Lin, Inspector of Xiang Province, held troops and would not obey orders; Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu were dispatched to lead troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xiangzhou inspector Wang Lin kept his army and defied orders; Zhou Wenyu and Hou Andu were sent against him.

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，梁帝進帝位相國，總百揆，封十郡為陳公，備九錫之禮，加璽紱，遠遊冠，綠綟綬，位在諸侯王上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinchou, the Liang Emperor advanced the Emperor to Chancellor, overseeing all affairs, enfeoffing ten commanderies as Duke of Chen with the full rites of the Nine Bestowments, adding seal and ribbon, the far-wandering cap, and green cord—rank above all feudal lords and kings.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the ninth month the Liang emperor made him Chancellor overseeing all affairs, enfeoffed ten commanderies as Duke of Chen with the Nine Bestowments, seal and ribbon, far-wandering cap, and green cord—rank above every prince.

sentences.zh: 策曰：大哉幹元，資日月以貞觀，至哉坤元，憑山川以載物。

translations.literal: The commission read: Great is the Creative Heaven, sustaining sun and moon in constant sight; utmost is the Receptive Earth, bearing mountains and rivers in their loads.
translations.idiomatic: The commission proclaimed: Great is the Creative Heaven, sustaining sun and moon in steadfast vision; utmost is the Receptive Earth, bearing mountains and rivers upon her back.

sentences.zh: 故惟天為大，陟配者欽明，惟王建國，翼輔者齊聖。

translations.literal: Therefore only Heaven is great, and he who ascends to match it is reverently bright; only the king establishes the state, and he who assists is equally sage.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Heaven alone is great, and he who mounts to match it shines with reverent brilliance; the king alone founds the realm, and his helper shares in sagehood.

sentences.zh: 是以文、武之佐，磻溪蘊其玉璜，堯、舜之臣，榮河鏤其金板！

translations.literal: Hence the aides of Wen and Wu concealed jade scepters at Panxi; the ministers of Yao and Shun engraved golden tablets at Ronghe!
translations.idiomatic: So the aides of Kings Wen and Wu hid jade scepters at Pan Stream; the ministers of Yao and Shun cut golden tablets at the Glory River!

sentences.zh: 況乎體得一之鴻姿，甯陽九之危厄，拯橫流于碣石，撲燎火於昆岡，驅馭于韋、彭，跨蹍于齊、晉，神功行而靡用，聖道運而無名者乎。

translations.literal: How much more one whose bearing holds the unity of the great swan, who calmed the ninefold peril, who rescued the drowning torrent at Jieshi, who smothered blazing fire at Kun Hill, who drove and bridled Wei and Peng, who trampled Qi and Jin—whose divine merit moved without display, whose sage way operated without name!
translations.idiomatic: How much more one who embodied the great swan's unity, stilled ninefold peril, rescued the drowning flood at Jieshi, smothered Kun Hill's blaze, drove like Wei and Peng, trampled Qi and Jin—whose divine merit moved unseen and whose sage way worked unnamed!

sentences.zh: 今將授公典策，其敬聽朕命：

translations.literal: Now I shall confer upon you the canonical commission; reverently hear my command:
translations.idiomatic: Now I confer the canonical commission upon you; hear my command with reverence:

sentences.zh: 日者，昊天不吊，鍾亂於我國家，網漏吞舟，強胡內贔，茫茫宇宙，惵惵黎元，方趾圓顱，萬不遺一。

translations.literal: Recently Heaven did not pity us; chaos struck our state and house; the net leaked great fish; fierce barbarians swelled within; the vast cosmos, the trembling masses—every square toe and round skull, not one in ten thousand spared.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Heaven withheld pity; chaos struck our house; the net let great fish escape; fierce barbarians swelled within; in the vast cosmos the people trembled—not one in ten thousand was spared.

sentences.zh: 太清否亢，橋山之痛以深，大寶屯如，平陽之禍相繼。

translations.literal: Taiqing's obstruction was extreme; the pain of Qiao Mountain ran deep; Dabao's difficulty piled up; Pingyang's calamities followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing's obstruction cut deep as Qiao Mountain's grief; Dabao's hardship piled up and Pingyang's disasters followed one upon another.

sentences.zh: 上宰膺運，康救黔黎，鞠旅于溟池之南，揚旌于桂嶺之北，縣三光於已墜，謐四海於群飛，光啟中興，蕩甯上國。

translations.literal: The chief minister received the mandate, comforted and saved the black-haired people, gathered armies south of the dark sea, raised banners north of Gui Ridge, hung the three luminaries where they had fallen, stilled the four seas amid flocking flight, opened the mid-restoration, and swept the upper realm to peace.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister took up the mandate, saved the people, gathered armies south of the dark sea and raised banners north of Gui Ridge, rehung the fallen three luminaries, stilled the four seas in flight, opened the mid-restoration, and swept the upper realm to peace.

sentences.zh: 此則公之大造於皇家者也。

translations.literal: This then is your great founding work for the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: This is your great founding work for the royal house.

sentences.zh: 既而天未悔禍，夷醜薦臻，南夏崩騰，西京蕩覆。

translations.literal: Then Heaven had not yet repented the calamity; barbarian ugliness came repeatedly; the southern summer collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven had not yet repented; barbarian hordes came again; the southern realm buckled and the western capital fell.

sentences.zh: 塚司昏撓，旁引寇讎，既見貶于桐宮，方謀危於漢閣，皇運已殆，何殊贅旒，中國搖然，非徒如線。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Masses was muddled and weak, drawing in enemy foes; already degraded to the Tung Palace, he plotted danger to the Han pavilion; the imperial fortune was already perilous, no different from a surplus tassel; the central land swayed, not merely like a thread.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Masses wavered and courted enemies; already shut in the Tung Palace, he plotted against the Han pavilion; the throne hung by a surplus tassel and the heartland swayed like a fraying thread.

sentences.zh: 公赫然投袂，匡救本朝，復莒齊都，平戎王室。

translations.literal: You boldly shook your sleeves, rescued and restored our dynasty, recovered Ju as Qi did its capital, pacified the barbarians and secured the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: You boldly shook out your sleeves, rescued the dynasty, recovered Ju as Qi had its capital, and secured the royal house against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 朕所以還膺寶曆，重履宸居，挹建武之風猷，歌宣王之雅頌。

translations.literal: Hence I again receive the precious calendar, again tread the imperial dwelling, draw in the style of Jianwu, sing the odes of King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I again mount the precious calendar, again tread the imperial hall, draw on Jianwu's style, and sing King Xuan's odes.

sentences.zh: 此又公之再造於皇家者也。

translations.literal: This again is your second founding of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: This again is your second founding of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 公應務之初，登庸惟始，孫、盧肇釁，越貊為災，番部阽危，勢將淪殄。

translations.literal: At the beginning when you took office, at the first appointment, Sun and Lu first raised rebellion; the Yue and Mo became disaster; the frontier tribes stood on the brink, their momentum about to perish.
translations.idiomatic: When first you took office, Sun and Lu raised rebellion; the Yue and Mo brought disaster; frontier tribes teetered on extinction.

sentences.zh: 公赤旗所指，祅壘洞開，白羽才撝，凶徒紛潰。

translations.literal: Where your red banner pointed, demon fortresses opened wide; where your white feather standard waved, vicious bands scattered in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Where your red banner pointed, demon forts gaped open; where your white-feather standard waved, vicious bands scattered.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 大同之末，邊政不修，李賁狂迷，竊我交、愛。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong, frontier governance was not maintained; Li Ben ran mad, stealing our Jiao and Ai.
translations.idiomatic: At Datong's end frontier rule collapsed; Li Ben ran wild and seized our Jiao and Ai.

sentences.zh: 公英暮雅算，電掃風行，馳禦樓船，直跨滄海。

translations.literal: You at dusk deployed elegant stratagems; lightning swept the wind's path; galloping tower-ships crossed the blue sea at a bound.
translations.idiomatic: You deployed elegant stratagems at dusk; lightning scoured the wind's path; tower-ships galloped straight across the blue sea.

sentences.zh: 三山獠洞，八角蠻陬，逖矣水寓之鄉，悠哉火山之國，馬援之所不屆，陶璜之所未開，莫不懼我王靈，爭朝邊候，歸賝天府，獻狀鴻臚。

translations.literal: The liao caves of Three Mountains, the barbarian corners of Eight Angles—the distant land of water-dwellers, the far country of fire-mountains—where Ma Yuan did not reach, where Tao Huang had not opened—all feared our king's spirit, vied to attend the frontier guard, sent tribute to the celestial treasury, and presented registers to the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Three Mountains' liao caves, Eight Angles' barbarian corners—lands of water-dwellers and fire-mountains where Ma Yuan never came and Tao Huang never opened—all feared our king's majesty, sought the frontier guard, sent tribute to the celestial treasury, and presented registers to the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 自寇虜陵江，宮闈幽辱，而番禺連率，本自諸夷，言得其朋，是懷同惡。

translations.literal: Since the invader barbarians crossed the river, the palace quarters suffered disgrace; yet the Panyu commander-in-chief was originally of the various barbarians—speaking, he found his fellows, and in heart he shared their evil.
translations.idiomatic: After invaders crossed the river and shamed the palace, the Panyu commander—himself of barbarian stock—found his kindred in speech and shared their evil in heart.

sentences.zh: 公仗此忠誠，乘機剿定，執沛令而釁鼓，平新野而據鞍。

translations.literal: You relied on this loyalty, seized the moment to strike and settle, executed the Pei magistrate and beat the warning drum, pacified Xinye and mounted the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: You relied on loyal purpose, seized the moment to strike, executed the Pei magistrate to beat the warning drum, pacified Xinye and mounted the saddle.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 世道初艱，方隅多難，公以國盜邊警，知無不為，恤是同盟，誅其丑類，南土黔黎，重保蘇息。

translations.literal: When the age's way was first difficult and the regions many in hardship, you because the state was robbed and the frontier alarmed knew nothing you would not do; you comforted the allied states and executed their ugly kind; the black-haired people of the southern land again found rest and recovery.
translations.idiomatic: When the age first turned hard and the regions troubled, you because the state was robbed and the frontier alarmed left nothing undone; you succored allies and executed villains until the southern people breathed again.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 長驅嶺嶠，夢想京畿，緣道酋豪，遞為榛梗，路養渠帥，全據大都，蓄聚逋逃，方謀阻亂。

translations.literal: Long-marching the mountain ridges, dreaming of the capital region, along the road local magnates successively became brambled barriers; Lu Yang's chieftain fully held the great metropolis, gathering fugitives, about to plot obstruction and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Long-marching the ridges yet dreaming of the capital, local magnates along the road became brambled barriers; Lu Yang's chieftain held the great city, gathered fugitives, and plotted obstruction.

sentences.zh: 公龍驤虎步，嘯吒風雲，山靡堅城，野無強陣，清祅氛于灨石，滅沴氣於雩都。

translations.literal: You dragon-surged and tiger-stepped, roaring at wind and cloud; mountains lost their strong walls, the wilds their strong formations; you cleared demon vapor at Gan Rock and extinguished pestilence at Yu Capital.
translations.idiomatic: You dragon-surged and tiger-stepped, roaring through wind and cloud; strong walls fell in the mountains, strong formations vanished in the wilds; you cleared demon vapor at Gan Rock and pestilence at Yu Capital.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 遷仕凶慝，屯據大皋，乞活類馬騰之軍，流人多杜弢之眾。

translations.literal: Qian Shi, vicious and wicked, encamped and held Dago, with armies like Ma Teng's beggar bands and floating populations like Du Tao's masses.
translations.idiomatic: The vicious Qian Shi held Dago with armies like Ma Teng's beggar bands and drifting masses like Du Tao's followers.

sentences.zh: 公坐揮三略，遙制六奇，義勇同心，貔貅騁力，雷奔電擊，穀靜山空，列郡無犬吠之驚，叢祠罷狐鳴之盜。

translations.literal: You sat wielding the Three Stratagems, remotely controlling the Six Wonders; righteous courage shared one heart; brave tigers exerted their strength; thunder ran and lightning struck; valleys stilled and mountains emptied; commanderies knew no dog-barking alarm; clustered shrines ceased fox-crying robbers.
translations.idiomatic: You sat wielding the Three Stratagems and remotely deployed the Six Wonders; righteous courage shared one heart and brave tigers strained their power; thunder ran and lightning struck until valleys stilled and mountains emptied; no commandery feared barking dogs and fox-crying shrines fell silent.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 王師討虜，次屆淪波，兵乏兼儲，士有饑色。

translations.literal: The royal army punished the invaders, halting at the sunken waves; troops lacked combined stores and soldiers had the color of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The royal army punished invaders at the sunken waves; troops lacked combined stores and soldiers wore hunger on their faces.

sentences.zh: 公回麾彭蠡，積穀巴丘，億庾之詠斯豐，壺漿之甿是眾。

translations.literal: You turned your banner at Poyang, piled grain at Baqiu; the ode of the hundred granaries was thus abundant; the mulberry folk with pot and broth were thus many.
translations.idiomatic: You turned your banner at Poyang and piled grain at Baqiu; granaries swelled with the ode's abundance and mulberry folk came with pot and broth.

sentences.zh: 故使三軍勇銳，百戰無前，承此兵糧，遂殄凶逆。

translations.literal: Therefore the three armies were brave and sharp, undefeated in a hundred battles; relying on this army grain, they then exterminated the vicious rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the three armies grew brave and sharp, unbeaten in a hundred fights; fed on this grain they exterminated the vicious rebels.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 盆壘猜攜，用淹戎略。

translations.literal: Pen fortress harbored suspicion and division, thereby delaying the military plan.
translations.idiomatic: Pen fortress nursed suspicion and division, delaying the military plan.

sentences.zh: 公志惟同獎，師克在和，屈禮交盟，神只感咽，故能使舟師並路，遠邇朋心。

translations.literal: Your will was solely mutual encouragement; the army conquers through harmony; you bent ritual to alliance; spirits and gods were moved to sighing; therefore you could make the fleet share one road and near and far share one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your will sought only mutual encouragement; armies conquer through harmony; you bent ritual to alliance until spirits sighed with emotion; thus fleet and land marched one road and near and far shared one heart.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 姑孰襟要，崤、函所憑，寇虜據其關梁，大盜負其扃鐍。

translations.literal: Gushu was strategically vital, relied upon like Xiao and Han passes; invader barbarians held its barrier-gates; great bandits bore its bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Gushu was strategically vital as Xiao and Han passes; invaders held its gates and great bandits its bolts.

sentences.zh: 公一校才撝，三雄並奮，左賢右角，沙潰土崩，鄂阪之隘斯開，夷庚之道無塞。

translations.literal: With one command your talent waved; three heroes strove together; left worthy, right corner—the sand broke and earth collapsed; the narrow pass of Eban opened and the road of Yigeng was unblocked.
translations.idiomatic: One wave of your command and three heroes strove; left worthy, right corner—sand broke and earth collapsed; Eban's narrow pass opened and Yigeng's road cleared.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 義軍大眾，俱集帝京，逆豎凶徒，猶屯皇邑。

translations.literal: The righteous army's great host all gathered at the imperial capital; rebellious villains and vicious bands still encamped in the royal city.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous host gathered at the imperial capital while rebel villains still camped in the royal city.

sentences.zh: 公回茲地軸，抗此天羅，曾不崇朝，俾無遺噍。

translations.literal: You turned this earth-axis, resisted this sky-net; in less than one morning you left none to swallow.
translations.idiomatic: You turned the earth-axis and resisted the sky-net; in less than one morning none remained to devour.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 內難初靜，諸侯出關，外郡傳烽，鮮卑犯塞。

translations.literal: When internal trouble was first stilled, feudal lords went out through the passes; outer commanderies passed beacon fires; Xianbei violated the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When internal trouble first stilled, lords marched out through the passes; outer commanderies lit beacons and Xianbei violated the frontier.

sentences.zh: 公舟師步甲，亙野橫江，殲厥群氐，遂殫封豕。

translations.literal: Your fleet and infantry armor stretched across field and river; you exterminated those Di clans and exhausted the great boar.
translations.idiomatic: Your fleet and foot stretched field and river; you exterminated the Di clans and exhausted the great boar.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 公克黜禍難，劬勞皇室，而孫、甯之黨，翻啟狄人，伊、洛之間，咸為虜戍，朝闇戎塵，夜喧胡鼓。

translations.literal: You overcame calamity and toil, labored for the imperial house; yet Sun and Ning's faction again opened the door to Di men; between Yi and Luo all became barbarian garrisons; at court dark with barbarian dust, at night loud with Hu drums.
translations.idiomatic: You overcame calamity and toiled for the throne, yet Sun and Ning's faction again opened the door to Di; between Yi and Luo all became barbarian garrisons; court dark with barbarian dust, night loud with Hu drums.

sentences.zh: 公三籌既畫，八陣斯張，裁舉靈鉟，亦抽金僕，咸俘丑類，悉反高墉。

translations.literal: Your three stratagems already drawn, the eight formations deployed; raising the spirit axe, also drawing the golden servant; all ugly kinds were captured and all returned to the high walls.
translations.idiomatic: Your three stratagems drawn and eight formations spread, you raised the spirit axe and drew the golden servant; every villain was taken and every wall reclaimed.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 任約叛渙，梟聲不悛，戎羯貪婪，狼心無改。

translations.literal: Ren Yue rebelled and scattered, his owl cry unrepentant; Rong and Jie were greedy, their wolf hearts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue rebelled and scattered with unrepentant owl cry; Rong and Jie stayed greedy with wolf hearts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 公左甄右落，箕張翼舒，掃是欃槍，驅其獫狁，投秦坑而盡沸，噎濉水而不流。

translations.literal: Your left wing and right rear, winnow-spread and wing-stretched, swept the comet-staff and drove the Xianyun; cast into Qin's pit they all boiled; choked the Sui waters they would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Left wing and right rear, winnow-spread and wing-stretched, you swept the comet-staff and drove the Xianyun; cast into Qin's pit they boiled; choked Sui's waters they ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 一相居中，自折彝鼎，五湖小守，妄懷同惡。

translations.literal: One minister held the center and himself broke the ritual tripod; a petty guard of the Five Lakes vainly harbored shared evil.
translations.idiomatic: One minister held the center and himself broke the ritual tripod; a petty Five Lakes guard vainly shared their evil.

sentences.zh: 公夙駕兼道，衣制杖戎，玉斧將揮，金鉦且戒，祅酋震懾，遽請灰釘。

translations.literal: You early drove double-quick, clothed for war with staff in hand; the jade axe about to swing, the golden gong already warning; demon chieftains trembled in awe and hastily requested execution by nail and ash.
translations.idiomatic: You early drove double-quick, clothed for war with staff in hand; jade axe ready to swing, golden gong already warning; demon chieftains trembled and hastily begged death by nail and ash.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 賊龕凶橫，陵虐具區，阻兵安忍，憑災怙亂。

translations.literal: The villain Kan was fierce and overbearing, tyrannizing the entire region, relying on troops and enduring cruelty, trusting disaster and clinging to chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The villain Du Kan was fierce and overbearing, tyrannizing the entire region, trusting arms and cruelty, clinging to chaos born of disaster.

sentences.zh: 公雖宗居汝、潁，世寓東南，眷言桑梓，公私憤切，戮此大憝，如烹小鮮。

translations.literal: Though you were clan-seated in Ru and Ying, dwelling for generations in the southeast, you spoke of native soil with public and private indignation, slaughtered this great villain as if cooking a small fish.
translations.idiomatic: Though your clan seat lay in Ru and Ying while your family dwelt in the southeast, you burned with public and private wrath for your homeland and slaughtered this great villain as easily as cooking a small fish.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 同姓有扈 ，頑凶不賓，憑藉宗盟，圖危社稷。

translations.literal: A kinsman of the same surname had followers, stubborn and fierce, not submitting as guest; relying on clan alliance, he plotted danger to the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of the same surname, stubborn and defiant, relied on clan alliance to threaten the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 公論兵於廟堂之上，決勝於尊俎之間，寇、賈、樊、滕，浮江下瀨，一朝翦撲，無待甸師。

translations.literal: You discussed warfare in the hall of the temple, decided victory between the honor cup and meat platter; Kou, Jia, Fan, and Teng floated down the river's rapids—in one morning they were cut down, with no need to wait for the capital army.
translations.idiomatic: You debated war in the temple hall and decided victory over the feast; Kou, Jia, Fan, and Teng floated down the river's rapids and were cut down in one morning without waiting for the capital army.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 豫章祅寇，依憑山澤，繕甲完聚，多曆歲時，結從連橫，爰洎交、廣。

translations.literal: The demon bandits of Yuzhang relied on mountains and marshes, repaired armor and gathered stores through many years, linking horizontal alliances even to Jiao and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang's demon bandits relied on mountains and marshes, repaired armor and hoarded stores for years, linking alliances even to Jiao and Guang.

sentences.zh: 呂嘉既獲，吳濞已鏦，命我還師，征其不恪，連營盡拔，偽黨斯禽。

translations.literal: When Lü Jia was already captured and Wu Pi already pierced, you ordered our army to return and campaign against their disobedience; linked camps were all uprooted and the false party was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Jia was taken and Wu Pi pierced, you ordered the army home and then marched against their disobedience; linked camps fell and the false party was captured.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 自八紘九野，瓜剖豆分，竊帝偷王，連州比縣。

translations.literal: From the eight cords and nine wilds, melon-sliced and bean-split, they stole imperial titles and false kings, linking prefectures and comparing counties.
translations.idiomatic: From the eight cords and nine wilds, realm carved like melon and bean, men stole thrones and false kings linked prefecture to prefecture.

sentences.zh: 公武靈已暢，文德又宣，折簡馳書，風猷斯遠。

translations.literal: Your martial spirit already flowed freely, your civil virtue again proclaimed; with folded letters and galloping dispatches, your wind and teaching reached far.
translations.idiomatic: Your martial spirit already flowed freely and civil virtue proclaimed anew; with folded letters and galloping dispatches your influence reached far.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 京師禍亂，亟積寒暄，雙闕低昂，九門寥豁。

translations.literal: The capital's calamity and chaos repeatedly accumulated cold and warm seasons; the paired towers hung low and high; the nine gates stood empty and open.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's calamity piled season upon season; the paired towers hung askew and the nine gates gaped empty.

sentences.zh: 公求衣昧旦，昃食高舂，興構宮闈，具瞻遐邇。

translations.literal: You sought robes at dawn's dimness, ate at sunset like the high pounding-stone, raised and constructed the palace quarters, gazed upon by near and far.
translations.idiomatic: You rose for robes at dawn's dimness and ate at sunset like the high pounding-stone, raised the palace quarters, and drew the gaze of near and far.

sentences.zh: 郊庠宗稷之典，六符十等之章，還聞泰始之風流，重睹永平之遺事。

translations.literal: The suburban schools' altars of soil and grain rites, the six tally-tokens and ten-rank seals—again one heard Taishi's elegance and again saw Yongping's surviving affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban schools, altars of soil and grain, six tally-tokens and ten-rank seals—again Taishi's elegance was heard and Yongping's surviving rites seen.

sentences.zh: 此又公之功也。

translations.literal: This again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: This too is your merit.

sentences.zh: 公有濟天下之勳，重之以明德，凝神體道，合德符天。

translations.literal: You had merit in saving the world, further weighted with bright virtue; concentrating spirit and embodying the Way, combining virtue to match Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: You had merit in saving the world, further weighted with bright virtue; concentrating spirit and embodying the Way, combining virtue to match Heaven.

sentences.zh: 用百姓以為心，隨萬機而成務，上德不德，無為以為。

translations.literal: Taking the hundred surnames as heart, following myriad affairs to accomplish tasks; highest virtue is non-virtue, non-action as action.
translations.idiomatic: You took the hundred surnames as your heart and followed myriad affairs to their completion; highest virtue is non-virtue, non-action as action.

sentences.zh: 夏長春生，顯仁藏用，功成化洽，樂奏咸雲，安上御人，禮兼文質。

translations.literal: Summer grows and spring generates, displaying benevolence and concealing use; merit accomplished and transformation harmonized, music played to Xian Cloud, settling the above and governing men, rites combining civil and martial.
translations.idiomatic: Summer grows and spring generates, displaying benevolence and concealing use; merit accomplished and transformation harmonized, music played to Universal Cloud, settling the above and governing men, rites joining civil and martial.

sentences.zh: 是以天無蘊寶，地有呈祥，既景煥于圖書，方葳蕤于史牒，高勳踰於象緯，積德冠于嵩、華，固無得而稱者矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven had no hidden treasure, Earth had displayed auspice; already bright in documents and books, about to flourish in historical records; high merit exceeded the asterisms and accumulated virtue crowned Song and Hua—truly nothing that could be named.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hid no treasure and Earth showed auspice; glory already blazed in documents and was about to flourish in records; high merit exceeded the asterisms and accumulated virtue crowned Song and Hua—truly beyond naming.

sentences.zh: 朕又聞之：前王宰世，茂賞尊賢，式樹藩長，總征群伯。

translations.literal: I also heard: former kings ruling the age richly rewarded and honored the worthy, erecting feudal chiefs to command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: I also heard: former kings ruling the age richly rewarded the worthy, erecting feudal chiefs to command the lords.

sentences.zh: 二南崇絕，四履遐曠，泱泱表海，祚土維齊；

translations.literal: The Two Souths were loftily set apart; four treadings reached far; vast it faced the sea; fief soil was Qi;
translations.idiomatic: The Two Souths stood loftily apart; four treadings reached far; vast it faced the sea and fief soil was Qi;

sentences.zh: 岩岩泰山，俾侯于魯。

translations.literal: Lofty lofty Mount Tai, making lords of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty, lofty Mount Tai, making lords of Lu.

sentences.zh: 況復經營宇宙，寧惟斷鼇足之功，弘濟蒼生，非直鑿龍門之險。

translations.literal: How much more managing the cosmos—surely not only the merit of severing the turtle's legs; broadly saving the black-haired people—not merely the peril of carving the Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: How much more managing the cosmos—not only severing the turtle's legs; broadly saving the people—not merely carving the Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 而疇庸報德，寂爾無聞，朕所以垂拱當寧，載懷慚悸者也。

translations.literal: Yet rewarding merit and repaying virtue was silently unheard; hence I bow in handling affairs at the throne, always bearing shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rewarding merit and repaying virtue went silently unheard; hence I bow at the throne handling affairs, always bearing shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 今授公相國，以南豫州之陳留南丹陽宣城、揚州之吳興東陽新安新甯、南徐州之義興、江州之鄱陽臨川十郡，封公為陳公。
